headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and cascading errors when Perplexity’s web-derived outputs feed Windsurf’s writable workspace and MCP-enabled execution.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Perplexity ingests live web content and browsing context, while Windsurf can consume clipboard/files and use MCP servers. That creates a plausible path where attacker-controlled web text from agent_a is treated as instructions by agent_b. Because the bridge is documented in both profiles and no provenance guard is shown, I rate this high rather than medium.
conditions: IF agent_b reads Perplexity-generated text from clipboard, files, or MCP output as instructions
IF agent_a returns raw web content that agent_b parses without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable copy/paste of agent_a outputs into agent_b prompts
Require explicit provenance tags before agent_b follows external text
Route Perplexity outputs through a human review step
Turn off MCP connections for the shared workflow
requires-engineering: add instruction/content separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent_a handles uploaded documents and browsing context, and agent_b reads and writes workspace files with local filesystem sharing across instances. Even without a proven shared directory, the pair can move sensitive document content from Perplexity into Windsurf’s workspace or model proxy. The blast radius is multiple work products, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF uploaded documents from agent_a are copied into agent_b workspace files
IF agent_b syncs shared local files containing agent_a browsing context or document excerpts
mitigations: Keep Perplexity and Windsurf on separate OS accounts
Do not upload sensitive documents to agent_a
Store agent_a outputs in a non-shared temp directory
Review workspace files before opening them in agent_b
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation between the tools

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent_b has unrestricted filesystem write, git modification, and broad network egress; agent_a has vendor-only egress and no host execution. If both touch the same project tree, Windsurf can overwrite or commit artifacts derived from Perplexity’s outputs without coordination. The overlap is dangerous by default because agent_b’s write surface is broad and locking is not documented.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace directory
IF agent_b auto-executes edits while agent_a is concurrently generating content
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate workspace
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git branches per agent
requires-engineering: add file-locking or orchestration locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity produces cited answers from live search, and Windsurf’s Cascade can act on tool outputs inside an editor loop. If Windsurf treats Perplexity’s answer as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into code changes, commits, or terminal actions. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so the downstream impact is high.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as a factual source without independent verification
IF agent_b auto-executes edits or terminal commands based on agent_a recommendations
mitigations: Require a second-source check before acting on agent_a outputs
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf
Limit agent_b to draft-only changes
Ask a human to verify citations before commit
requires-engineering: add confidence gating between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity touches uploaded documents and browsing context, while Windsurf handles source code, open files, and optional model-provider keys. If regulated or proprietary data is moved from agent_a into agent_b’s local workspace or model proxy, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated documents from agent_a are opened in agent_b
IF agent_b sends workspace contents to a third-party model proxy or MCP server
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Windsurf workspaces
Use redacted copies for agent_b
Review retention settings for both vendors
Avoid placing secrets in files opened by agent_b
requires-engineering: formalize a data-handling policy for the pair
